title: the diagram of the state machine is written out of the code
intent: The wave D1 of the track D: the diagram of the state machine of the site is not a drawing, but a reading of the code.  The machine of the kernel is a table in the code -- the states are `yeah-state-list' and the cells are `yeah-loop--raw-transitions' -- and the diagram of that machine is written out of the table, so that the two cannot drift apart: the table changed, the diagram is another one.  (1) The generator lives in `lib/yeah-state-diagram.el' and knows how to say the diagram and nothing else; the source is a function of the code and of nothing else -- no date, no hash, no order of its own, and the same code gives the same bytes.  (2) The state the machine starts in is the state the first cell of the table comes from.  (3) `scripts/dev' gains the subcommand `state-diagram', and the pipeline of the diagrams calls the same generation before it draws anything: a generation that failed ends the pipeline with its own answer, and nothing is drawn.  (4) The source of the diagram is committed (`site/diagrams/state-machine.puml'), so that the check can compare the bytes of the repository with the bytes that the code writes.  (5) The check measures every part of the promise: the file of the repository against the file that a copy of the kernel writes, a cell added to the table of the copy, a state added to the list of the states of the copy, the coverage of the machine (the numbers are read out of the code and are not written in the check), the two themes of the picture, a tree without a kernel, and the promise that the tree of the repository is never written.  The claim `the-state-diagram-comes-from-the-code' is new.
objection: The claim is about a source and not about a picture: the wave commits no SVG (the pictures of the site are waves D3 and D4), and the check draws its pictures in a temporary tree, so the tree of the repository is never written -- the check compares the listing of `site/diagrams' and of `site/assets/diagrams' before and after itself.  The generator reads the table of the code and not the picture of it: PlantUML does not read a dash in an identifier, and a name with a dash in it (`post-decide') keeps its text as the label of the state and gets an identifier of its own (`post_decide'), and the ends of the arrows speak that identifier -- the picture shows the names of the machine as they are, and the source names them twice.  The check compares bytes, and a source written by a hand and a source that the code wrote are the same file only when they are the same bytes: the control of the claim changes the table and does not regenerate the file, and the check names the drift.  The pipeline requires the kernel now, and a tree without a kernel answers with the code 3 and draws nothing: that is the price of generating the source before the rendering, and the price is paid by a tree that has no kernel at all.  The generation of the source is a step of the instrument of the author and not a build step of the site: the published site carries the ready SVG, and a site that has no Emacs is not broken.  The number of the cells of the table is checked by the kernel itself when it loads, and the copy of the kernel in the check carries the counter with it: a check that changed the table without the counter would not load the kernel at all, and that is a verdict of the kernel and not a verdict of the check.
refuted_by: the diagram of the repository is not the file that the generator writes from the current code, or the generator does not read the table of the transitions, or the generator does not read the list of the states, or the diagram does not carry every cell and every state of the machine, or the pipeline does not draw the machine in both themes, or the pipeline answers with the code 0 when the machine cannot be generated, or the tree of the repository is written, or the control of the claim does not make the check fail by its own assertion
note: The claim of the wave is new and not an amendment: the id `the-state-diagram-comes-from-the-code' is new, and the promise of the wave 83 about the pipeline (`the-diagram-pipeline-renders-both-themes') is not touched -- the pipeline renders every diagram of the tree in both themes as before, and the tree of the diagrams has one diagram more.  Fifteen controls were applied to copies of the tree on 2026-11-20 -- eight by the writer of the wave and seven more by the parent, and the parent's seven were made independently of the report of the writer.  Every one of them ended with the verdict the control asked for.  (1) The honest tree -- the code 0, in 3 seconds.  (2) The control of the claim -- the cell `(deciding stream-end . post-decide)' becomes `(deciding stream-end . accumulating)' and the diagram is not regenerated: «the diagram of the repository is not the diagram that the code writes: the table of the transitions changed and the diagram was not written again»; code 1.  (3) The source of the repository is changed by hand -- the same verdict; code 1.  (4) The generator is made blind to the table (`(dolist (cell nil)') and the source of the repository is regenerated to match it: «the diagram of the changed table has no arrow of the new cell: the generator does not read the table»; code 1.  (5) The skin of the dark theme is broken -- the pipeline of the check answers not 0; code 1.  (6) The generator writes nothing and answers with the code 0 -- the check names it; code 1.  (7) A tree without a kernel -- the generation answers with the code 3 and says why; code 3.  (8) The check of the wave 83 on the tree of the wave 84 -- the code 0, and its own control (the loop of the themes loses the dark one) bites still; code 1.  The measurement of the wave: the module is 100 lines and 4.4 kB, the check is 397 lines and 16.7 kB, and it goes in 3.5 seconds; the diagram carries the eleven states of the machine and the thirty-one arrows of the table, and the pipeline renders two pictures of one diagram.  The deviations from the plan are named in the plan itself: PlantUML does not read a dash in an identifier, and the name of the state keeps its text as a label; `@startuml state-machine' gives the picture the name of the diagram and not the name of the file, and the pipeline learned to find the picture that a diagram which names itself writes; the pipeline requires the kernel now; and the assertion of the wave 83 about the tree of the sources was rewritten, because the pipeline writes the generated source into the tree it draws from.
